sourceChecks.claim: Checked S3 key naming: bucket-local identifiers, flat namespace, prefixes and console folders. GCS objects followup explicitly confirms copy/delete non-atomic simulated-folder rename; Welcome defines bytes and Content-Type metadata. Supports the scoped model.

Checked S3 Welcome object/key model and single-key consistency boundary: no cross-key atomic updates. Application database publication and orphan recovery are justified architectural deductions from separate operations, not a documented cross-system transaction.

Checked GCS objects immutability and atomic replacement, plus S3 Welcome single-key old-or-new reads. GCS Object Versioning table and S3 Versioning distinguish retained versions from current bytes and permanent replacement when protections are disabled.

Checked GCS consistency read/list guarantees, retryable failure, caches and non-atomic batches; S3 Welcome confirms strong reads/lists and nondeterministic acknowledgment arrival. GCS objects.list pageToken documentation shows changing listings are not a frozen snapshot; prefix filters names.

Checked GCS preconditions: generation match, live-object absence with zero, failed conditions, and retry races after network interruptions. S3 conditional-writes confirms If-None-Match/If-Match differences and overwrite protection. A condition failure establishes no ownership of stored bytes; lost response remains uncertain.

Checked GCS availability/durability definitions and redundant storage before confirmation; S3 Welcome and DataDurability establish successful stored writes, replication and class-dependent zone coverage. GCS/S3 versioning and consistency followups establish explicit protection, finite retention and configuration propagation; response delivery is distinct.

Checked GCS IAM principal-role-permission-resource model and S3 Welcome requester/action/resource authorization. GCS consistency explicitly documents delayed access revocation. Separate application ownership checks and keeping broad credentials from clients follow from the credential boundary.

Checked AWS comparison on object units, direct block writes and shared filesystem operations. GCS immutability supports replacement trade-off; S3 FAQ permits small objects. CloudFront Introduction confirms edge caching, lower latency and S3 origin. Database/application responsibilities follow the taught separate data model.
